points.title: 音乐神童
points.description: 弗朗茨·李斯特于1811年10月22日出生于匈牙利雷丁的一个德语家庭。父亲亚当·李斯特是一位业余音乐家，发现了儿子的音乐天赋并开始教他钢琴。李斯特9岁就在匈牙利多个城市公开演出，展现出惊人的钢琴技巧。1821年，12岁的李斯特随父亲前往维也纳，师从著名钢琴教育家卡尔·车尔尼学习，并在维也纳宫廷进行演出，获得贝多芬的认可。这段早期经历奠定了李斯特作为钢琴神童的基础，也塑造了他对音乐的执着追求。
points.descriptionEn: Franz Liszt was born on October 22, 1811, in Raiding, Hungary, to a German-speaking family. His father Adam Liszt, an amateur musician, discovered his son's musical talent and began teaching him piano. By age 9, Liszt was giving public concerts in various Hungarian cities, displaying extraordinary piano skills. In 1821, at age 12, Liszt moved with his father to Vienna, where he studied under renowned piano pedagogue Carl Czerny and performed at the Vienna court, gaining Beethoven's recognition. This early period established Liszt as a musical prodigy and shaped his lifelong dedication to music.

points.title: 巴黎崛起
points.description: 1823年，李斯特全家迁往巴黎。在这里，李斯特不仅继续钢琴演奏事业，还开始作曲。他结识了多位文学和艺术界名人，包括维克多·雨果、海涅和乔治·桑。1830年代，李斯特成为巴黎社交界的宠儿，以其华丽的钢琴技巧和创新的演奏风格闻名。他创作了《十二首超技练习曲》等作品，并开创了独奏音乐会的新形式。这一时期，李斯特还与玛丽·达古尔伯爵夫人有了一段著名的恋情，这段关系对他的创作产生了深远影响。
points.descriptionEn: In 1823, Liszt's family moved to Paris. Here, Liszt not only continued his piano performance career but also began composing. He met numerous literary and artistic figures, including Victor Hugo, Heinrich Heine, and George Sand. During the 1830s, Liszt became a darling of Parisian high society, renowned for his brilliant piano technique and innovative performance style. He works like the 'Twelve Transcendental Études' and pioneered the concept of the solo piano recital. During this period, Liszt also had a famous affair with Countess Marie d'Agoult, which profoundly influenced his compositions.

points.title: 钢琴之王
points.description: 1839年至1847年间，李斯特开始了欧洲各地的巡回演出，足迹遍及德国、奥地利、意大利、俄罗斯等多个国家。他的音乐会场场爆满，观众为之疯狂，人们称他为'钢琴之王'。这一时期，李斯特的演奏技巧达到了巅峰，他创新性地将钢琴作为独奏乐器，开创了现代钢琴独奏音乐会的形式。同时，他创作了《匈牙利狂想曲》系列作品，这些作品融合了匈牙利民间音乐元素，成为他的代表作。巡演的成功使李斯特成为当时最著名的音乐家之一，也积累了可观的财富。
points.descriptionEn: Between 1839 and 1847, Liszt embarked on extensive concert tours across Europe, visiting Germany, Austria, Italy, Russia, and other countries. His concerts were sold-out events, with audiences going wild, earning him the title 'King of the Piano.' During this period, Liszt's performance technique reached its zenith, as he innovatively established the piano as a solo instrument, pioneering the modern piano recital format. He also composed his 'Hungarian Rhapsodies,' which incorporated Hungarian folk elements and became his signature works. The success of these tours made Liszt one of the most famous musicians of his time and brought him considerable wealth.

points.title: 魏玛时期
points.description: 1848年，李斯特接受魏玛大公的邀请，成为魏玛宫廷乐长，结束了长达十年的巡演生活。在魏玛的13年间，李斯特专注于作曲和指挥工作，创作了《浮士德交响曲》、《但丁交响曲》等重要作品，并积极推广当时的新兴音乐家如瓦格纳、柏辽兹等。他还组织了魏玛音乐节，使魏玛成为欧洲音乐中心之一。这一时期，李斯特的音乐风格从炫技转向更深刻的表达，创作了许多具有革新意义的作品。同时，他与卡洛琳·冯·赛因-维特根斯坦公主的关系成为他生活中的重要部分，这段关系持续了多年。
points.descriptionEn: In 1848, Liszt accepted an invitation from Grand Duke Carl Alexander of Weimar to become Kapellmeister at the Weimar court, ending his decade-long touring career. During his 13 years in Weimar, Liszt focused on composition and conducting, creating major works like the 'Faust Symphony' and 'Dante Symphony,' while actively promoting emerging composers such as Wagner and Berlioz. He organized the Weimar Music Festival, establishing Weimar as one of Europe's musical centers. During this period, Liszt's musical style evolved from virtuosic display to more profound expression, producing many innovative works. His relationship with Princess Caroline von Sayn-Wittgenstein also became a significant part of his life during these years.

points.title: 宗教转变
points.description: 1861年，李斯特移居罗马，并进入修道院，成为一名神职人员。他接受了低级神职，但没有成为神父。在罗马期间，李斯特创作了大量宗教音乐作品，包括《基督》清唱剧、《圣伊丽莎白传奇》等。这一时期，他的音乐风格更加内省和精神性，反映了他的宗教信仰。尽管过着宗教生活，李斯特仍然保持与音乐界的联系，指导年轻音乐家，包括汉斯·冯·彪罗和理查·施特劳斯。1865年，他在梵蒂冈被教皇庇护九世授予'阿博特'头衔，进一步巩固了他在宗教界的地位。
points.descriptionEn: In 1861, Liszt moved to Rome and entered a monastery, becoming a cleric. He received minor orders but did not become a priest. During his time in Rome, Liszt composed numerous religious works, including the oratorio 'Christus' and 'Legend of Saint Elizabeth.' This period saw his musical style become more introspective and spiritual, reflecting his religious faith. Despite his religious life, Liszt maintained connections with the music world, mentoring young musicians including Hans von Bülow and Richard Strauss. In 1865, he was granted the title of Abbé by Pope Pius IX at the Vatican, further solidifying his position in religious circles.

points.title: 晚年教学
points.description: 1869年后，李斯特开始了他最后的'流浪生活'，在布达佩斯、魏玛和罗马之间往返。1875年，他协助建立了布达佩斯音乐学院（现李斯特音乐学院）并担任院长。这一时期，李斯特主要致力于教学工作，培养了一大批杰出的音乐家，包括弗雷德里克·肖邦、亚历山大·齐尔品等。他的教学理念强调技巧与艺术的结合，对后世钢琴教育产生深远影响。1881年，李斯特在魏玛遭遇严重事故，导致健康恶化。1886年7月31日，李斯特在德国拜罗伊特参加瓦格纳音乐节期间去世，享年74岁。他的去世标志着浪漫主义音乐时代的结束。
points.descriptionEn: After 1869, Liszt began his final 'wandering life,' traveling between Budapest, Weimar, and Rome. In 1875, he helped establish the Budapest Academy of Music (now Liszt Academy of Music) and served as its director. During this period, Liszt primarily devoted himself to teaching, nurturing a generation of distinguished musicians including Frederic Chopin and Alexander Scriabin. His teaching philosophy emphasized the integration of technique and art, profoundly influencing future piano education. In 1881, Liszt suffered a serious accident in Weimar that led to declining health. On July 31, 1886, Liszt died in Bayreuth, Germany, while attending the Wagner Festival, at the age of 74. His death marked the end of the Romantic era in music.

supporter.zh: 李斯特被誉为钢琴史上最伟大的革新者之一，他彻底改变了钢琴演奏艺术，将钢琴从伴奏乐器提升为独奏乐器。他的高超技巧和创新的演奏风格为后世钢琴家树立了标杆。作为作曲家，他开创了交响诗这一音乐形式，对瓦格纳等人的创作产生深远影响。李斯特还是一位杰出的教师，培养了一大批优秀音乐家，他的教学理念至今仍影响着钢琴教育。此外，他积极推广其他作曲家的作品，特别是瓦格纳，体现了无私的艺术奉献精神。
supporter.en: Liszt is regarded as one of the greatest innovators in piano history, revolutionizing piano performance art and elevating the piano from an accompanying instrument to a solo instrument. His exceptional technique and innovative performance style set standards for future generations of pianists. As a composer, he pioneered the symphonic poem form and profoundly influenced composers like Wagner. Liszt was also an outstanding teacher, nurturing numerous talented musicians, and his pedagogical philosophy continues to influence piano education today. Additionally, he actively promoted the works of other composers, particularly Wagner, demonstrating selfless artistic dedication.

critic.zh: 批评者认为李斯特的音乐有时过于华丽炫技，缺乏深度和内涵。他的部分作品被指责为肤浅的展示技巧而非真正的艺术表达。此外，李斯特的个人生活备受争议，他的风流韵事和频繁的恋爱关系被一些人视为道德上的缺陷。在音乐理念上，他支持瓦格纳的'整体艺术'观念，这一理念后来被纳粹德国利用，成为其文化宣传的一部分。批评者还指出，李斯特晚年转向宗教音乐，被认为是对他早期创新精神的背离，显示出艺术上的保守倾向。
critic.en: Critics argue that Liszt's music is sometimes overly ornate and virtuosic, lacking depth and substance. Some of his works are criticized as superficial displays of technique rather than genuine artistic expression. Additionally, Liszt's personal life was controversial, with his numerous affairs and relationships viewed by some as moral failings. Musically, his support for Wagner's 'total art' concept was later exploited by Nazi Germany for propaganda purposes. Critics also note that Liszt's turn to religious music in his later years is seen as a departure from his earlier innovative spirit, suggesting artistic conservatism.

objective.zh: 从历史角度看，李斯特是连接古典主义与浪漫主义音乐的关键人物，也是19世纪音乐文化的重要推动者。他的音乐创新和表演技巧对后世产生了深远影响，许多现代钢琴演奏技巧都可以追溯到他的实践。在流行文化中，李斯特常被描绘为浪漫主义天才的典型形象，他的传奇人生和才华使其成为音乐史上最具魅力的人物之一。他的作品，尤其是《匈牙利狂想曲》，至今仍是音乐会上的热门曲目，显示出持久的艺术生命力。李斯特的一生展现了艺术家在个人追求、社会责任和艺术创新之间的复杂平衡。
objective.en: From a historical perspective, Liszt was a pivotal figure connecting Classical and Romantic music and a significant driving force in 19th-century musical culture. His musical innovations and performance techniques had a profound impact on later generations, with many modern piano techniques tracing back to his practices. In popular culture, Liszt is often portrayed as the epitome of the Romantic genius, his legendary life and talent making him one of the most fascinating figures in music history. His works, particularly the 'Hungarian Rhapsodies,' remain concert staples today, demonstrating enduring artistic vitality. Liszt's life exemplifies the complex balance between personal pursuit, social responsibility, and artistic innovation.

self.zh: 音乐是灵魂的语言，它表达无法言说的事物。
self.en: Music is the language of the soul, it expresses that which cannot be put into words.

others.zh: 李斯特是钢琴的帕格尼尼，他不仅演奏钢琴，他本身就是钢琴。
others.en: Liszt is the Paganini of the piano, he doesn't just play the piano, he is the piano.
